title: Carbonara
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The spaghetti, silken tofu, miso, Portobello Bacon, olive oil, turmeric, lemon juice, black pepper, water, and salt contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active is true because the sauce is built around silken tofu and pasta-water emulsification, while Portobello Bacon supplies smoke and chew without animal fat or cholesterol. The dish uses plant-based structure, controlled fat, and technique rather than eggs, cheese, or cured pork.
intro: Carbonara belongs to Rome, where pasta, eggs, cheese, cured pork, and black pepper become a glossy sauce through heat control and pasta water. This version moves in that direction through different ingredients and techniques. Portobello bacon brings smoke, chew, and browned depth; silken tofu gives the sauce body; turmeric adds warm color and a subtle earthy note; and black pepper keeps the whole dish pointed toward carbonara.

stepGroups.title: Blend the sauce
items: Blend the silken tofu ({{quantity:silken-tofu}}), white miso ({{quantity:white-miso}}), ground turmeric ({{quantity:ground-turmeric}}), black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper-sauce}}), fresh lemon juice ({{quantity:lemon-juice}}), and hot pasta cooking water ({{quantity:hot-pasta-cooking-water-sauce}}) until completely smooth.

stepGroups.title: Cook the pasta
items: Bring the water ({{quantity:water}}) to a boil.
Add the kosher salt ({{quantity:kosher-salt-pasta}}) and spaghetti ({{quantity:spaghetti}}).
Cook until the spaghetti is just shy of al dente.
Reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta cooking water, then drain the spaghetti.

stepGroups.title: Build the carbonara
items: Heat the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil}}) in a wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the coarsely ground black pepper ({{quantity:coarsely-ground-black-pepper}}) and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Add the drained spaghetti and toss to coat in the pepper oil.
Add the blended tofu sauce and toss constantly, adding small splashes of reserved pasta cooking water as needed, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the spaghetti.
Fold in most of the re-crisped Portobello Bacon ({{quantity:portobello-bacon}}), saving some for the top.
Let the pasta rest for 1 minute so the sauce settles.
Serve immediately with the remaining Portobello Bacon scattered over the top.
